description:
`issue claim-next --filter` is accepted but ignored, so a worker asking for a narrowed candidate set claims the highest-priority ready issue regardless of the filter. Agents that rely on the flag take work outside their scope, and malformed filters pass silently.

## Background

`CommandExecutor::claim_next` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:737`) takes the filter as `_filter` and never reads it; it ranks `query_ready` by priority and claims the first candidate. The CLI declares `-f, --filter` with no help text (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:1196`) and passes it through at `crates/jit/src/main.rs:4002`. `docs/concepts/core-model.md` (around lines 1172 and 1246) documents the flag as accepted but not applied.

The same boolean query language already drives `issue update --filter` through `QueryFilter::parse` (`crates/jit/src/query_engine/mod.rs`).

Reproduction in a fresh git repository with jit initialized:

```bash
jit issue create "Alpha" --type task --priority critical   # then set state ready
jit issue create "Beta"  --type epic --priority low        # then set state ready
jit issue claim-next agent:w1 --filter 'label:type:epic' --json
# claims Alpha (type:task), not Beta
jit issue claim-next agent:w2 --filter 'garbage %%%' --json
# succeeds and claims Beta instead of rejecting the filter
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `issue claim-next --filter <expr>` claims only a ready, unassigned, unblocked issue that matches `<expr>` in the query language `issue update --filter` accepts, choosing the highest-priority match.
- [hard] REQ-02: When no ready issue matches the filter, the command fails with the not-found error and claims nothing, even if non-matching ready issues exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: A filter that does not parse fails with an invalid-argument error before any issue is claimed.
- [hard] REQ-04: `issue claim-next --help` describes the `--filter` argument and its syntax.
- [hard] REQ-05: The documentation no longer describes `--filter` as ignored, and its claim-next examples show filtered claiming.
- [hard] REQ-06: A regression test proves a filter excluding the highest-priority ready issue causes a lower-priority matching issue to be claimed.

## Notes

Reuse the existing `QueryFilter` mechanism; a claim-specific filter syntax would duplicate it (`@/inv/convention-convergence`).
title: Apply the claim-next filter when choosing which issue to claim
